topics.summary: Application of derivatives to evaluate limits yielding 0/0 or ±∞/∞.
topics.worked_example:
Evaluate \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin(3x)}{x}.
Solution: Direct substitution gives 0/0. Differentiate numerator (3\cos(3x)) and denominator (1). \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{3\cos(3x)}{1} = 3(1) = 3.

topics.summary: First-order equations of the form dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x).
key_formulas: y \cdot I(x) = \int Q(x) \cdot I(x) dx + C
topics.worked_example:
Solve dy/dx + 2y = e^{-x}.
P(x) = 2, so I(x) = e^{\int 2 dx} = e^{2x}.
Multiply: e^{2x} \frac{dy}{dx} + 2e^{2x}y = e^x \implies \frac{d}{dx}[y e^{2x}] = e^x.
Integrate: y e^{2x} = e^x + C \implies y = e^{-x} + C e^{-2x}.
